en.name: Thomas Aquinas
en.summary: The "Angelic Doctor," whose Summa Theologica remains the single most influential work of Catholic philosophy and theology.
en.body: Born to a noble Italian family, Thomas Aquinas scandalised his relatives by joining the recently founded Dominican order rather than pursuing a more prestigious path. As a friar and professor in Paris and Naples, he undertook the vast project of synthesising Christian theology with the newly rediscovered philosophy of Aristotle, producing the Summa Theologica — an unfinished but monumental systematic treatment of God, creation, ethics, and Christ. Declared a Doctor of the Church, his thought ("Thomism") remains the reference point for much of Catholic philosophy.
